newsitem.title: GERMANY: AgrEvo-96 op profit to hit 200 million marks.
newsitem.headline: AgrEvo-96 op profit to hit 200 million marks.

text.p: German AgrEvo GmbH, the world's second-largest crop protection group, said on Friday it expects its 1996 operating profit to be around 200 million marks.

AgrEvo, which is jointly-owned by German chemical companies Hoechst and Schering, said its 1996 operating profit already includes provisions and charges relating to a major acquisition the company made in August.
AgrEvo also expects 1996 sales will have risen by over 11 percent to around 3.75 billion marks, compared with 3.4 billion marks in 1995.
In 1995, the group's operating profit was 147 million marks.
The sales rise was largely due to an increase in volume sales, improved currency relationships and a small increase in prices.
AgrEvo said foreign exchange considerations barely affected 1996's figures. The companies results in 1995 were seriously dented by foreign exchange market turmoil in that year,
The company also said sales climbed 12.2 percent in the first nine months of 1996 compared to the year-ago figure, but declined to give give an exact figure.
Operating profit in the first nine months of 1996 "improved markedly", AgrEvo said, again declining to give a figure.
AgrEvo expected its herbicide business to grow by 11 percent in 1996, its insecticide business by ten percent and its fungicide business to grow by nine percent.
It expected five percent growth in its health business in 1996.

In August AgrEvo bought a 95 percent stake in Plant Genetic Systems International N.V., a Dutch-Belgian biotechnology company. The company paid around one billion marks for the stake and has placed a bid to buy the remaining shares in PGS.
AgrEvo will spend around 400 million marks on research in 1996 and invested around 150 million marks in tangible assets excluding investment in PGS.
